free_tier.stated: EUR 6.00/month for U1 in Moldova: 1 vCore, 1.5 GB DDR4, 10 GB NVMe, 'Shared 100 Mbps', IPv4. Next rows: U2 at EUR 10.00/month with 2 vCores, 4 GB DDR4 and 40 GB NVMe, in Moldova at 100 Mbps and in the Netherlands, Sweden, Bulgaria, Switzerland, France, England and Romania at 1 Gbps; U4 at EUR 16.00/month with 4 vCores, 8 GB and 80 GB NVMe, Moldova at 100 Mbps and the same seven locations at 1 Gbps. The billing selector offers 1 month, 3 months, 6 months and yearly.

egress.terms: the vendor table states only a port: 'Shared 100 Mbps' in Moldova, 'Shared 1 Gbps' in the seven other locations. No monthly byte allowance and no overage price are printed. The tracker states 31,641 GB/month, which is consistent with the 100 Mbps port sustained for about 29 days
egress.free_allowance: 31,641 GB per month as the tracker states it; the vendor page states no monthly allowance

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.tooling: not stated on the page read: the pricing table, a price-tier filter (entry level under EUR 90, mid tier EUR 90 to 195, top tier above EUR 195) and the billing-cycle selector are all the page documents. No API, control-panel name or image list appears in the extract
record.chaining: EUR 6.00 for 1.5 GB is the lowest entry price among evaluated providers, but 100 Mbps and 10 GB of disk make it a control-plane host for a scheduler, DNS secondary or webhook receiver rather than a host that moves bytes; U2 at EUR 10.00 doubles the disk and buys 1 Gbps in every location except Moldova, which is the row to take if throughput matters.

limits.value: 31,641 GB a month is the allowance the tracker states, and it is the 'Shared 100 Mbps' port the vendor prices, run continuously: 100 Mbps sustained for about 29 days is that byte count. The vendor table prints no monthly byte allowance, so the quota and the port are the same wall and the port is what actually bites; no overage price exists because nothing beyond the port is sold. Moldova is the only location at 100 Mbps, and the FAQ states the 1 Gbps upgrade is confined to selected European locations.

record.notes: The vendor table and the tracker agree on price, cores, disk and location, and the vendor's '1.5 GB' and the tracker's '1,536 MB RAM' are the same figure. The tracker's 31,641 GB is read here as a conversion of the 100 Mbps port rather than as a published quota, because the vendor page sells a port and no bytes; that reading is arithmetic and is the one claim in this record that is not quoted. The one hit is compute/fossvps, which cites a LowEndTalk thread titled 'fossvps-updates-free-server-for-open-source-developers-from-alexhost-hosteroid-and-st-hosting' in an evidence row - a lead about a free program for open-source developers that was not read, so free_tier_kind stays none here.
